churn_timeline.event: Onboarded. Eric opens the group, five staff introduce themselves over four days. She submits the intake form the same afternoon.

Previous team found still logged into her OnlyFans. Mayson tells her to change the password; she posts the new credentials straight into the group chat. Nobody flags it, nothing is rotated. Her booked kickoff call also silently fails and only happens because she chases her own booking.
Day 3: subscribers collapse from 60-70/day to 4. Fred explains it honestly and promises a push. This is the last performance number she is ever given.
She reports all her socials appear shadowbanned. No diagnosis, no escalation; she works around it herself via her personal TikTok.
She asks about the paid promo Derrek sold her. Closed with an @-tag to someone not in the conversation. Never started, never mentioned again.
First invoice unpayable: no phone on the Zelle, then no email, then the wrong email. Invoice #1 is abandoned on 6/10 after nine days of failed attempts on our rails.
She asks for the Miami/Orlando shoot from the pitch. 6/8: 'following up with them now'. Never raised again by anyone.
She discovers 13 of her voice notes were never processed - the client doing our QA.
Invoice #2 arrives on a third rail (Mercury). She disputes commission on ~$583 of self-run live earnings. 'Let me work with the team' is followed by six days of silence.
Fourth rail (Chase); the Mercury link is admitted incorrect on 6/23; she pays the corrected $931.81 the same evening.
'Hi all those leaks are still up' - the day after a graphic claimed 197 infringements removed. She re-sends ten fresh links within eight minutes.
Identical complaint, second time in 48 hours. Nothing escalates; 6/29 'let me check on this with the team', 7/1 a generic process explanation.
Fifth banking change in 33 days ('last change I promise!'), same week as her loudest unresolved complaint.
She stops asking and sets her own terms: calculates the invoice herself, deducts her live earnings, sends $981.
Sends the wire, then resigns 21 minutes later: 'I'm going to take over my account and work independently'. Volunteers a final balance and photographs the figure (msg id 316). Nobody ever replies.
Mica's reel inspo and Michelle's leak report fire on schedule, four days after the resignation. Then 23 consecutive days of zero ALTR messages.
First post-churn human contact, 27 days late: a request for her earning statements so we can bill her. 8/4: 'Just making sure you saw this' - the last message in the chat.

Post-mortem refetch: settlement NEVER closed. 59 days since her last message, 30 days of total dead air, final invoice 50 days past cadence and still unissued, exit-balance photo still untranscribed. The 8/28 deadline (issue or write off by 9/4) arrives tomorrow with zero action taken.

warning_signs_missed: 2026-05-30 - Subscribers fell from 60-70/day to 4 on day 3. We explained it once and then never reported another growth or revenue number for the remaining 37 days. A client who stops receiving numbers stops being able to justify the fee.

2026-05-31 - 'I think like all my socials are shadow banned' was treated as a conversational aside rather than a platform incident. She then spent five weeks producing content into damaged accounts and self-diagnosing.

2026-06-02 - A question about promo Derrek sold her in the pitch was closed with an @-tag to someone not in the conversation. An unfulfilled pre-sale promise with no owner is the classic churn seed, and nothing in our process reopens it.
2026-06-11 - The client caught our failure, not us: 13 voice notes had silently failed to upload. When the client is doing our QA, our internal checks have already failed.

2026-06-15 - A commission dispute is a repricing conversation. She flagged that she wanted her own live earnings excluded; we never wrote a policy, so on 7/2 she simply started deducting it herself. A client who has begun setting her own terms has already half-left.

2026-06-26 and 2026-06-28 - The same complaint twice in 48 hours, both times answered with a status graphic or a process explanation instead of a per-link result. Repeat of an identical complaint is the most reliable churn predictor in this dataset and no rule escalates it.
2026-07-01 - Our third bank change in 30 days landed in the same week as her loudest unresolved complaint. Nobody was looking at the account as a whole, so nobody saw the friction compounding.
2026-07-05 - She was still doing our DMCA intake for us the day before she quit. Her remaining effort was all going into the one thing we had not fixed - that is what an exhausted client looks like.

2026-07-10 - Two templated broadcasts fired four days after she resigned. The signal we missed here is about ourselves: our outbound is on autopilot and nobody reads these chats, which is why a resignation could sit unanswered for 59 days.
top_fix: Give every account one named owner whose job is closing complaints with evidence rather than routing them - and make that owner's churn duties non-optional: reply to a resignation within 24 hours, and issue the final invoice from ALTR's own records within 7 days. Hannah's two loudest issues (leaks still live, the promised paid promo) were each answered with a graphic or an @-tag and dropped; her resignation and her volunteered exit payment then sat unowned for five consecutive weekly reviews. This account should now be closed: transcribe msg id 316, issue the 7/1-7/7 invoice off ALTR's OF records with a 14-day pay-by via her known off-Telegram contacts, or write it off on 2026-09-04 as previously agreed - and stop producing reports about it.
